newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says may intervene on forex if wide deviation.
newsitem.headline: MOF says may intervene on forex if wide deviation.

text.p: Intervention in foreign exchange markets by Japanese authorities is possible if exchange rates deviate greatly from economic fundamentals, senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara told a parliamentary committee on Wednesday.
Asked how the finance minister decided whether to intervene in the currency market, Sakakibara said the decision was based on whether exchange rates were in line with economic fundamentals.
"Intervention is possible in cases in which rates deviate greatly from economic fundamentals," said Sakakibara, the director-general of MOF's International Finance Bureau.

Sakakibara was responding to questions about Japanese laws concerning foreign exchange transactions which state that the finance minister is responsible for trying to maintain stability in the currency market.
